study_name.notes: No canonical study name/identifier provided in paper; ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT02217384 is available but not a standard study name format.

pmid.notes: Extracted from paper_id field provided with submission.

target_condition.evidence_quote: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is an eating disorder with a high mortality.

country.evidence_quote: only included Danish Caucasian women with AN cases, recruited from three specialized centres in Denmark

body_site.evidence_quote: Shotgun metagenomics and metabolomics were performed on faecal and serum samples
body_site.notes: Faecal samples analyzed via shotgun metagenomics; also serum samples but primary microbiota analysis is fecal.

dna_extraction_kit.evidence_quote: DNA extraction from aliquots of faecal samples was performed following IHMS SOP P7 V2
dna_extraction_kit.section: Methods — Faecal sample collection and DNA extraction
dna_extraction_kit.notes: Supplementary Figure 7 workflow shows NucleoSpin soil mini kit (MACHEREY-NAGEL) used for mouse experiments; for human samples, IHMS SOP P7 V2 protocol referenced but specific kit name not explicitly stated in main methods. However, text states 'DNA extraction... following IHMS SOP P7 V2' which is a standardized protocol. Mapping to nearest enum value is uncertain; marked as 'other' would be more accurate but NorgenBiotek is closest match if IHMS protocol aligns with NorgenBiotek products.

ncbi_accession.notes: No NCBI SRA/ENA accessions provided in paper text.

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: Purified and amplified DNA fragment libraries were sequenced using the Ion Proton Sequencer
sequencing_platform.notes: Human samples sequenced on Ion Proton; mouse 16S amplicon sequencing used Illumina MiSeq but primary metagenomics platform is Ion Proton.

age.notes: Age reported as ranges and means for study cohort but not for individual samples. Study recruited women aged ~18-53 per EDI-3 validation, but specific per-participant ages not provided in extractable form.

age_group.evidence_quote: EDI-3 was designed for use in females aged 13–53 years. Age-matched healthy controls
age_group.notes: Study restricted to adult women per recruitment criteria and clinical context of specialized eating disorder centres. Age group inferred as Adult (>=18 yrs) since EDI-3 used clinically and study enrolled treatment-seeking cases, but exact per-sample ages not reported.

ancestry.notes: Explicitly stated as Caucasian; Danish ethnicity implies Northern European ancestry.

sex.evidence_quote: only included Danish Caucasian women with AN cases
sex.notes: All human study participants were female by design.

control.notes: Granularity is sample_level but control status (Case vs Study Control) cannot be determined per sample from provided text; study includes 77 AN cases and 70 healthy controls but individual sample-level control assignment not provided.

subject_id.notes: Individual subject identifiers not reported in paper; only aggregate counts (n=77 AN, n=70 HC) provided.

sample_id.notes: Individual sample identifiers not reported; samples referenced only by study group membership.

zigosity.notes: Twin zygosity not discussed in this study.

age_min.notes: Paper does not provide minimum age; only reports age-matched controls and states female donors aged 20, 22, 20 yr and HC aged 20, 22, 21 yr in FMT experiments. [age_min/age_max set from schema age-bound rule]

age_max.notes: Paper does not provide maximum age; only specific ages for FMT donors. [age_min/age_max set from schema age-bound rule]

age_years.notes: Study population described as age-matched females but mean/median age not reported in main text or abstract.

antibiotics_current_use.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria comprised antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months
antibiotics_current_use.notes: Exclusion criterion for both AN cases and healthy controls; all enrolled participants had no antibiotics within 3 months.

bmi.notes: Individual BMI values not provided; study-level BMI comparison shows AN cases were much leaner with lower BMI than controls, but exact aggregate value not stated in abstract or main text.

dietary_restriction.evidence_quote: energy-restricted feeding to mirror AN eating behaviour
dietary_restriction.notes: Described in animal experiments (FMT mice on 30% calorie-restricted diet); human AN characterized by reduced food intake.

disease.evidence_quote: 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females
disease.notes: Primary condition; study includes both AN-RS (restricting type) and AN-BP (binge-eating/purging type) subtypes.

disease_details.evidence_quote: It can be classified into two subtypes, the common restricting (AN-RS) type and the less prevalent binge-eating or purging (AN-BP) type
disease_details.notes: Study enrolled n=56 AN-RS and n=21 AN-BP cases out of 77 total AN participants.

disease_response_orr.notes: Not applicable; ORR is for oncology treatment response. This is a mechanistic/observational microbiota study, not a treatment response trial.

disease_response_pfs.notes: Not applicable; PFS is an oncology metric. This study does not measure treatment progression.

disease_response_pfs_month.notes: Not applicable; not an oncology study.

disease_response_recist.notes: Not applicable; RECIST is for solid tumor response. This is a microbiota/mechanistic study, not an oncology trial.

feces_phenotype.evidence_quote: Shotgun metagenomics and metabolomics were performed on faecal and serum samples
feces_phenotype.notes: Stool phenotypes profiled via metagenomics (bacterial/viral) and metabolomics.

fmt_id.evidence_quote: faecal microbiota from AN cases to germ-free mice
fmt_id.notes: Study identifiers for FMT recipients; 6 donors (3 AN-RS cases, 3 HC) transplanted to 3 independent litters of female germ-free mice; n=10 recipients per group.

fmt_role.evidence_quote: faecal samples from randomly selected subsets of three patients with AN...and three HC...used to colonize 6-week-old female GF littermates
fmt_role.notes: Paper describes donors (3 AN cases, 3 HC controls) and germ-free recipient mice; FMT procedure performed at day 1-3.

hla.notes: HLA typing not performed or reported.

neonatal_birth_weight.notes: Not applicable; study enrolled adult female AN patients, not neonates.

neonatal_delivery_procedure.notes: Not reported; study does not collect neonatal delivery data.

neonatal_feeding_method.notes: Not reported for human participants; animal studies only report standard chow diet.

neonatal_gestational_age.notes: Not applicable; study enrolled adult female participants, not neonates.

neonatal_preterm_birth.notes: Not applicable; study enrolled adult female participants.

obgyn_birth_control.evidence_quote: regular medication of any kind apart from birth control pills
obgyn_birth_control.notes: Birth control pill use was permitted in healthy controls (not an exclusion); no data provided on actual usage prevalence.

obgyn_menopause.notes: Not reported; study enrolled females but menopausal status not documented.

obgyn_pregnancy.notes: Not explicitly reported; no exclusion criterion or mention of pregnancy status.

smoker.evidence_quote: covariates including age, BMI, smoking and multiple drug intake were corrected
smoker.notes: Smoking status collected as a covariate in regression models; paper does not report prevalence or distribution of smoking status among participants.

treatment.evidence_quote: Medication included selective serotonin re-uptake inhibitors, antipsychotics and benzodiazepines
treatment.notes: These medications were deconfounded in analyses; actual prevalence and individual medication names not specified.

tumor_staging_ajcc.notes: Not applicable; this is not a cancer study.

tumor_staging_tnm.notes: Not applicable; this is not a cancer study.

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: serum concentrations of glucose and insulin, higher insulin sensitivity as estimated by homoeostatic model assessment for insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) and lower serum C-reactive protein
biomarker_name.section: Results — Phenotypes of women with AN and controls
biomarker_name.notes: Multiple biomarkers measured in human cohort and mouse experiments. Some are metabolites, some are genes/transcripts, some are proteins.

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: serum concentrations of glucose and insulin; mRNA levels of the indicated mice genes
biomarker_unit.notes: Specific numerical units not consistently reported for all biomarkers in the paper text

biomarker_value.notes: Paper reports associations and fold-changes but not absolute biomarker values in main text; detailed values in Supplementary Tables

disease_response_os.notes: Overall survival not measured; this is a cross-sectional microbiome study, not a survival study

disease_response_os_unit.notes: Not applicable; no overall survival data collected

ecog_performance_status.notes: ECOG performance status not assessed in this microbiome study

value: altered bacterial composition at phylum level with reduction in Bacteroidota and Actinobacteriota
higher β-diversity at genus and species level
85 overlapping amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) between human donors and GF mouse recipients
45 (53%) altered ASVs in donors transferred to recipients
31 conserved metabolites between human donors and mouse recipients
alterations of 19 of 31 (61%) transferred metabolites from human to mouse
higher viral richness (Chao1) and diversity (Shannon) in AN
219 viral–bacterial interactions in HC versus 84 in AN
31 viral species enriched or decreased in AN
25 of 30 increased viral species in AN were Lactococcus phages
feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: At the phylum level, AN microbiota samples were characterized by a reduction in Bacteroidota and Actinobacteriota; higher β-diversity of AN microbiome at genus level; 85 overlapping amplicon sequence variants (ASVs)
feces_phenotype_value.section: Results — Gut microbiota composition is altered in AN; Lactococcus phages and weakened trans-kingdom interactions in AN
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Multiple fecal microbiota phenotypes measured including taxonomy, diversity metrics, virome characteristics, and transfers in FMT experiments

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Not applicable; study of anorexia nervosa pathogenesis, not cancer

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Not applicable; no tumor measurements in this study

value: 77 female AN cases with DSM-5 diagnosis; 70 age-matched healthy female controls
Danish Caucasian women only; recruited September 2014 to July 2016
Exclusion: antibiotics/antifungals within 3 months, acute/chronic somatic diseases or infections
Controls: BMI 18.5-25 kg/m², no regular medications except birth control, no antibiotics within 3 months
AN cases: restricting (AN-RS) subtype (n=56) and binge-eating/purging (AN-BP) subtype (n=21)
Inpatients received safe weight restoration at 2.0-3.0% per week under multidisciplinary care
Outpatients received individual diet plans with 40-50% carbohydrate, 30-40% fat, 20-25% protein
Shotgun metagenomics performed on fecal samples; metabolomics on serum samples
FMT experiments: germ-free Swiss Webster mice colonized with fecal samples from 3 AN cases and 3 healthy controls
Mice underwent 30% energy-restricted diet for 3 weeks to mimic AN eating behavior
6-week-old female germ-free mice; 8, 6, and 6 littermates per litter respectively
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females; Danish Caucasian women; Exclusion criteria comprised antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months
uncurated_metadata.section: Methods — Study participants; Results — Animal experiments
uncurated_metadata.notes: Key study design and participant characteristics relevant to understanding the research context

host_species.evidence_quote: 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females; female germ-free Swiss Webster mice
host_species.notes: Study includes both human participants (women) and mouse model experiments (female Mus musculus)

samples.feces_phenotype_value: altered bacterial composition at phylum level with reduction in Bacteroidota and Actinobacteriota; higher β-diversity at genus and species level; higher prevalence of Ruminococcacea-enterotype (R-enterotype); 85 overlapping amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) between human donors and GF mouse recipients; 45 (53%) altered ASVs in donors transferred to recipients; 31 conserved metabolites between human donors and mouse recipients; alterations of 19 of 31 (61%) transferred metabolites from human to mouse; higher viral richness (Chao1) and diversity (Shannon) in AN; 219 viral–bacterial interactions in HC versus 84 in AN; 31 viral species enriched or decreased in AN; 25 of 30 increased viral species in AN were Lactococcus phages
samples.uncurated_metadata: 77 female AN cases with DSM-5 diagnosis; 70 age-matched healthy female controls; Danish Caucasian women only; recruited September 2014 to July 2016; Exclusion: antibiotics/antifungals within 3 months, acute/chronic somatic diseases or infections; Controls: BMI 18.5-25 kg/m², no regular medications except birth control, no antibiotics within 3 months; AN cases: restricting (AN-RS) subtype (n=56) and binge-eating/purging (AN-BP) subtype (n=21); Inpatients received safe weight restoration at 2.0-3.0% per week under multidisciplinary care; Outpatients received individual diet plans with 40-50% carbohydrate, 30-40% fat, 20-25% protein; Shotgun metagenomics performed on fecal samples; metabolomics on serum samples; FMT experiments: germ-free Swiss Webster mice colonized with fecal samples from 3 AN cases and 3 healthy controls; Mice underwent 30% energy-restricted diet for 3 weeks to mimic AN eating behavior; 6-week-old female germ-free mice; 8, 6, and 6 littermates per litter respectively

extraction_warnings: Granularity set to sample_level per schema guidance, but paper does not provide per-sample rows with individual identifiers. Data are reported at cohort level (n=77 AN, n=70 HC) with aggregate statistics. No per-sample metadata table is available for extraction.
Control field cannot be populated per-sample without individual subject allocation data. Paper describes two groups (AN cases and HC controls) but does not list sample-level case/control assignments.
Subject_id and sample_id not reported; all analyses are cohort-level or subgroup-level (by AN subtype, treatment status, etc.).
Age reported only as cohort-level range/mean, not per-participant.
DNA extraction kit: IHMS SOP P7 V2 protocol specified but specific kit product name not explicitly stated for human samples. Enum mapping is uncertain.
Sequencing platform for metagenomics is Ion Proton (human), but mouse amplicon sequencing used Illumina MiSeq; primary platform for metagenomics listed.
Batch 1 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.
age_years not reported at study level; FMT donor ages (20, 22, 20 yr for AN; 20, 22, 21 yr for HC) are available but cohort-level mean/median age not provided
bmi: Study reports AN cases were much leaner than controls but exact aggregate BMI values not stated in abstract or methods
smoker: Collected as covariate but prevalence distribution not reported
obgyn_birth_control: Birth control pills permitted as exception to medication exclusion but actual usage not quantified
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.
ECOG performance status, overall survival, and tumor measurements are not applicable to this anorexia nervosa microbiome study and were returned as 'not_reported'
Biomarker_value field reports associations and statistical measures rather than absolute values; raw data values are in Supplementary Tables not provided in text

Study has subgroups (AN-RS vs AN-BP subtypes; inpatients vs outpatients) but requested schema does not include fields to capture subgroup-specific microbiota or metabolite values; granularity set to 'study_level' per schema instructions
Multiple biomarker categories measured (serum metabolites, genes/transcripts, proteins) without consistent unit reporting in main text
